findings.title: Phpinfo Use
findings.description: The phpinfo() function is used to output information about PHP's configuration, which can reveal sensitive details about the environment, such as file paths and database credentials. findings.fix_hint: Remove the phpinfo() function call to prevent information disclosure

attack_chains.title: SQLi to RCE
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses SQL injection to extract database credentials, then uses these credentials to gain remote code execution via a tainted exec call, achieving persistence on the system. This allows them to exfiltrate sensitive data and maintain access. The attacker starts by exploiting a SQL injection vulnerability in the 'vulnerabilities/bac/source/low.php' file.
steps: Step 1: attacker extracts database credentials using SQL injection in 'vulnerabilities/bac/source/low.php' (finding '3c17f9f3')
Step 2: attacker uses extracted credentials to gain remote code execution via a tainted exec call in 'vulnerabilities/exec/source/low.php' (finding '3293713c')
Step 3: attacker achieves persistence and exfiltrates sensitive data
attack_chains.remediation: Input validation and sanitization for all user-provided data in 'vulnerabilities/bac/source/low.php' to prevent SQL injection

attack_chains.title: Phpinfo to SQLi
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses phpinfo to reveal database configuration details, then uses this information to perform a SQL injection attack, extracting sensitive data from the database. The attacker starts by accessing the 'phpinfo.php' file to gather database configuration details.
steps: Step 1: attacker reveals database configuration using phpinfo in 'phpinfo.php' (finding 'b1cb93f0')
Step 2: attacker uses revealed configuration to perform SQL injection in 'vulnerabilities/sqli/source/low.php' (finding 'e49ce043')
Step 3: attacker extracts sensitive data from the database
attack_chains.remediation: Remove or restrict access to 'phpinfo.php' to prevent database configuration disclosure

attack_chains.title: Tainted Filename to RCE
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses a tainted filename to execute arbitrary code on the system, then uses this access to exfiltrate sensitive data. The attacker starts by exploiting a tainted filename vulnerability in the 'instructions.php' file.
steps: Step 1: attacker executes arbitrary code using a tainted filename in 'instructions.php' (finding 'e619346c')
Step 2: attacker uses executed code to gain remote code execution via a tainted exec call in 'vulnerabilities/exec/source/low.php' (finding '21c00964')
attack_chains.remediation: Validate and sanitize all filenames and user-provided data in 'instructions.php' to prevent arbitrary code execution
